answer: Per-agent resource grove. Each identity gets a private quota of scarce compute and a violet-tagged rate slot on a shared ledger. Minting a clone requires provisioning a fresh grove from a bounded pool; when pool occupancy rises, every allocation shrinks and a marble-timestamped cooldown blocks new slots. A clone therefore yields less compute than the parent consumed to spawn it, while the attacker pays full provisioning cost for each marginal identity. Net expected value per duplicate stays strictly below zero.
